note: Read scribe.json for what a claim is and how it is rated. Every signal here was derived by running the recorded code rather than from the design, and two of them moved as a result.

claims.policy: money moved between your own accounts
claims.statement: Money moved between your own accounts is left out of the totals.

probe.present_means: the total is the spending alone, with the two transfer legs outside it
probe.absent_means: the total has moved, so money between your own accounts is being counted

claims.statement: A row recorded twice is counted once, matched on its date, its amount and its merchant.

probe.present_means: a coffee and a pastry of the same amount on the same day are both counted
probe.absent_means: two different merchants of the same amount on one day are merged, so the match no longer uses the merchant

claims.policy: which month a transaction counts in
claims.statement: A transaction counts in the month it was made, not the month the bank posted it.

probe.present_means: a transaction made in January and posted in February counts in February
probe.absent_means: a transaction made in January and posted in February counts in January

claims.statement: A merchant that matches no rule goes to the uncategorised bucket, and the run finishes.

probe.present_means: an unmatched merchant lands in the uncategorised bucket and a summary is produced
probe.absent_means: the run refuses over an unmatched merchant, so there is no summary at all

claims.statement: A refund is netted against its own category rather than reported separately.

probe.present_means: the refund is netted against groceries
probe.absent_means: the refund is not netted against groceries
